text:
zoe-peopleops: Heads-up  International conversion: candidate (Lina) finishing internship in Toronto wants FT start 10/1. Manager requesting L3 base above midpoint, $15k relocation reimbursement, $10k sign-on, and prorated RSUs. Need comp exception routing + tax/gross-up check.

rahul-mgr: Context: Lina owns linux perf tooling; strong local offers in Toronto market. Relocation critical because family needs local school support; we want to lock her early. Prefer 18-month clawback on sign-on+relocation.

keiko-recruit: Candidate verbally agreed pending written offer. Key ask: benefits active day one and assistance with temporary housing.

zoe-peopleops: Please paste manager justification and headcount code. Also flag that this is Canada (ON). International hires often need immigration + payroll checks.

rahul-mgr: Justification: "critical infra ownership, immediate impact, multiple active offers." Headcount: ENG-2026-10-TOR.

finance-ops: Quick budget note: base + sign-on + relocation = meaningful hiring premium. Need GL tag and approval to classify relocation as reimbursable vs taxable gross-up. Tag ENG-2026-10-TOR.

payroll-bot: payroll note: In Canada, relocation reimbursements are generally taxable unless structured as employer-paid moving expenses meeting CRA rules; gross-up may be required. Sign-on treated as taxable income. If company gross-ups relocation, this increases cash cost. Please confirm which approach.

legal-bot: International clawback: Canadian enforcement is different; 18-month clawback may be harder to enforce depending on province and reason for repayment. Recommend 12 months for CA/ON; 18 only with strong business justification (rare). Also verify provincial employment standards for deductions.

immigrations-ops: Immigration note: Lina is currently on a co-op/work permit. For FT we need LMIA-exempt work permit or PR sponsorship path; timeline can be 4-8 weeks. Start date 10/1 might be tight. Recommend offer contingent on successful permit and include expected start window.

keiko-recruit: Candidate is Canadian citizen? She is an international student with work authorization via co-op but not PR. We need immigration ops to advise.

immigrations-ops: If she is international student on post-grad work permit (PGWP) she can start FT without LMIA. If still on co-op only, need next permit. Need candidate confirmation.

zoe-peopleops: Routing plan: recruiting lead -> finance -> people-ops exceptions committee -> legal -> payroll (for gross-up decision) -> immigration ops. Also equity team for prorated RSUs.

equity-team: Equity proration: we can prorate to quarter boundaries. With Toronto start, currency conversion/time zone fine. Need final grant size to compute tax withholding impact.

rahul-mgr: Proposed terms (manager draft):

```
Base: CAD 150,000/year (L3, above midpoint)
Sign-on: CAD 10,000 one-time (proposed 18-month clawback)
Relocation: CAD 15,000 reimbursable (request gross-up)
Equity: 1,800 RSUs, prorated first year, standard 1y cliff
Start window: target 2026-10-01 (contingent on work authorization)
Benefits: enroll from start date
```

zoe-peopleops: Please also note currency in packet and include cash-flow impact in CAD and USD. Finance, do you want cost amortized over 12 months?

finance-ops: Yes amortize sign-on and relocation over first 12 months for budget calc; include gross-up delta if company covers tax. Approve to committee for review if manager justification included.

payroll-bot: If company agrees to gross-up relocation, provide gross-up calculation method; payroll will compute employer tax liabilities and supplemental withholding. This will add ~30-40% to relocation cost depending on provincial rates.

legal-bot: For clawback language in Canada: recommend 12 months, repayment terms, exceptions (termination without cause, layoffs). If manager insists on 18 months, include stronger justification and consult local counsel. Also ensure offer includes contingency for work authorization.

keiko-recruit: Candidate asks whether we can front-load temporary housing stipend for first 30 days. That would be taxable; recruitment team asks if we can issue as reimbursable receipts to minimize tax.

payroll-bot: Reimbursable receipts: if moving expenses meet CRA conditions, reimbursements may be non-taxable; temporary housing stipends typically taxable unless tied to moving relocation rules. Recommend receipts and relocation vendor involvement.

zoe-peopleops: I'll prepare exception packet with manager justification, GL code ENG-2026-10-TOR, budget calc (CAD+USD), proposed 12 vs 18-month clawback rationale, and contingency language for work authorization. Routing now.

finance-ops: Proceed to people-ops exceptions committee. We'll attach cost amortization and gross-up scenarios.

legal-bot: I'll prepare two clawback templates (12-month standard, 18-month escalated with justification) and a work authorization contingency clause.

immigrations-ops: I'll check candidate permit details ASAP; if she has PGWP start 10/1 likely fine. If not, push start window accordingly.

keiko-recruit: Candidate ETA for signed offer: within 72 hours after receiving final terms. Please keep thread short. :pray:

zoe-peopleops: Committee meeting tomorrow morning. If approved, we'll finalize offer with payroll gross-up decision and issue same day. Archive thread after acceptance.
